title: End-to-End 4-Bit Training
author: Jack Cook, with others at Thinking Machines (Thinking Machines Lab)
updated_note: the page's metadata gives a modification on 25 November; the only change in the text since the first archived copy (14 November) is a credit, "Like Quartet II" becoming "Like TetraJet-v2 and Quartet II" (compared in Provenance)
more_note: Its interactive figures (the bit-level NVFP4 widget, the 16 x 16 tile figures, the Hadamard scatter) are worth opening there; this page redraws none of them.
takeaway: On one model, Inkling 2 Small (594B total, 17B active, a mixture of experts), Thinking Machines ran the expert layers' forward matmuls in NVFP4 and their backward matmuls in MXFP8 re-quantised with stochastic rounding, and sent expert-parallel traffic in 4.5 and 8.25 bits a value; in their largest jobs they report about 8% faster pretraining at about 2% compute efficiency and about 20% faster RL with no discernible difference in reward, both against full MXFP8, with no seeds, loss curves or reward curves published.
verdict: Believe the mechanisms: each fix (column scales after a transpose, unbiased re-quantisation by stochastic rounding, an 8-bit combine after a Hadamard rotation) follows published work, checks out by arithmetic and does what the toy on this page shows, and two small replications on one B200 see the same direction. Treat the sizes as vendor figures for one model: no curves, seeds or baseline loss, an "8% speedup" that does not say whether it is time or throughput, and a cost that, netted, leaves about 5.5% less time to the same loss (derived).

responses.t: 4bit-training-b200: 4-bit training, tested on one NVIDIA B200
responses.by: Raj Dandekar and Vizuara AI Labs
responses.n: An 840M GPT on TinyStories, 2,000 steps: NVFP4 forward with an 8-bit backward reached validation loss 1.6912 and 1.6910 (two seeds) against 1.6886 and 1.6873 in BF16; steps 1.006 to 1.035 times faster than all-8-bit at widths 2,048 to 8,192. Backward FP8 with per-tensor scales, not MXFP8; no Four Over Six.

responses.t: [Feature] End-to-end 4-bit MoE training: NVFP4 forward, MXFP8 backward, quantized EP comm (radixark/miles #4952)
responses.n: Plans the recipe in six phases for Miles (Megatron, Transformer Engine); the stochastic MXFP8 backward needs a Transformer Engine fork. Its current Inkling trainer runs experts in BF16 with fake-quantised weights, part of a 0.019 train-rollout log-probability gap. Open, no pull request, on 27 November.

responses.t: RL on the released NVFP4 weights (a comment on miles #4952)
responses.n: RL on Inkling 2 Mini from the release weights (fp32 master, fake-quantised experts): Adam steps of about 1e-6 against NVFP4 grid steps of 1e-3 to 1e-2, so almost no expert code flips, and learning about as slow as with experts frozen. Asks for full-precision master weights; unanswered on 27 November.

responses.t: looped-transformer-4bit: replicating Inkling 2 Mini with 4-bit forward passes
responses.n: A 10.6M model on TinyStories, laptop, emulated: 4-bit forward with MXFP8 backward 1.214 nats per byte at step 300 against 1.196 in full precision (one run each). Rounds the backward re-quantisation to nearest, because Transformer Engine's MXFP8 quantiser has no stochastic option.

since.n: Apache 2.0 weights, NVFP4 the main release and an MXFP8 checkpoint beside it; no full-precision weights. It says the model "was pretrained, midtrained and post-trained in NVFP4", which is shorter than the post: only the expert layers' forward matmuls were NVFP4.

since.t: Inkling 2 Small in NVIDIA NeMo AutoModel
since.n: Lists the NVFP4 release as NVFP4 experts in layers 0 to 39 and MXFP8 in layers 40 to 47: the last 8 of 48 layers, 16.7%, the post's "last 16.6%". The native implementation is not yet merged.
The first open-source framework to plan the full recipe; open with no linked pull request when checked.

resources.t: Pretraining Large Language Models with NVFP4
resources.n: The recipe this one departs from: NVFP4 in all three matmuls of a 12B model for 10T tokens, with 16 x 16 weight tiles, Hadamard transforms on the weight gradient and stochastic rounding on gradients.

resources.t: Quartet II: Accurate LLM Pre-Training in NVFP4 by Improved Unbiased Gradient Estimation
resources.n: Re-quantises the forward pass's tensors for the backward pass so the gradient estimate stays unbiased; one of the two works the post credits.

resources.t: TetraJet-v2: Accurate NVFP4 Training for Large Language Models with Oscillation Suppression and Outlier Control
resources.n: The other credited source of re-quantisation from the forward tensors.

resources.t: Four Over Six: More Accurate NVFP4 Quantization with Adaptive Block Scaling
resources.by: Cook et al., 2025 (the post's author is its first author)
resources.n: Lets each block choose whether its largest value maps to 4 or to 6, whichever loses less; the recipe uses it on activations, not weights.

resources.t: NVFP4 for RL (Four Over Six for RL weights and activations)
resources.by: Ziang Li and others at humans&, July 2026 (third-party)
resources.n: The write-up the post recommends: a dequantised backward, Four Over Six on weights too, and selected layers in high precision removed gradient-norm spikes in five RL runs.

resources.t: Stable FP4 Training via Transposition-Invariant Block Quantization
resources.n: Fixes the same transpose mismatch the other way, with 2D blocks that are the same in both directions, plus stochastic rounding: under 1.3% degradation up to 7B dense and a 30B MoE, 100B tokens. Not cited by the post.

resources.t: Recipes for Pre-training LLMs with MXFP8
resources.n: The 8-bit baseline every number in the post is measured against.
MXFP8 and MXFP4: blocks of 32 values sharing one power-of-two (E8M0) scale.

kb.n: Owns the formats (E2M1, E4M3, MXFP8, NVFP4), block scales and the Bit explorer (sections 1 and 2), the Hadamard rotation (Fig. 8) and every 4-bit training recipe side by side (section 6, Fig. 10).
Owns how bits encode a float, round-to-nearest against stochastic rounding (section 2), and master weights (section 9).

kb.t: RL for LLMs: RLHF, GRPO, RLVR
kb.n: Why a sampler and a trainer that compute different probabilities turn on-policy RL off-policy, and the low-precision rollout recipes (TRACE, TRIAGE).

kb.t: bf16 Rounding Silently Discards Most RL Policy Updates (Fair Cast)
kb.n: Updates smaller than half a grid step vanish under round-to-nearest: the same arithmetic as the question on the released NVFP4 weights.
Routers, dispatch and combine, expert parallelism: the layer the recipe quantises.
NVLink 5 at 900 GB/s each way and NVL72 domains: the link the combine was waiting on.
Blackwell Ultra's FP4 rate (15 PF against B200's 10) and tensor memory.
FP8 training with 128 x 128 weight blocks, the FP8 form of the square-tile idea the post rejects for NVFP4.
Inkling 2 Small and Inkling 2 Mini: sizes, licence and benchmark readings.
The issue that first listed the post, with the NVFP4 rare-fact recall paper beside it.
